title: Indexes, Pagination & Transactions
summary: Make slow lookups use indexes (proved with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN), page through data with keyset pagination, and move stock atomically so a failure never leaves the database half-updated.

hints.test_customer_orders_query_uses_index: The query filters on customer_id (equality) and order_date (range). A composite index on (customer_id, order_date) lets SQLite SEARCH instead of SCAN, with the equality column first.
hints.test_product_lookup_uses_index: order_items' primary key starts with order_id, so it can't help a lookup by product_id. Add an index whose first column is product_id.
hints.test_create_indexes_is_idempotent: Use CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS so running the migration twice is safe.
hints.test_keyset_pagination: Use WHERE order_id > ? ORDER BY order_id LIMIT ?. Each page starts after the last id of the previous page, so there's no OFFSET to re-scan.
hints.test_transfer_moves_stock: Decrement the source and increment the destination inside one transaction, then return the two new quantities.
hints.test_transfer_creates_destination_row: Use INSERT … ON CONFLICT(warehouse, product_id) DO UPDATE SET qty = qty + excluded.qty so a missing destination row is created.
hints.test_insufficient_stock_rolls_back: Check the source quantity first and raise ValueError. Make sure nothing was written and no transaction is left open.
hints.test_invalid_quantity_rejected: Reject qty <= 0 with ValueError before touching the database.
hints.test_failure_midway_is_atomic: Wrap both writes in `with conn:`. It commits on success and rolls back if anything inside raises, including the second write.
hints.test_queries_are_parameterized: Never build SQL with f-strings. Pass values as parameters (?), so names with quotes work and injection attempts are just data.
